rationale: A implements each operation with a plain, idiomatic loop, which is clear and efficient. Its only blemish is reverse using insert(0), which is quadratic. B builds everything on a recursive append that slices list1 at each level. That makes append quadratic, and because map, filter, concat and reverse all call it, every one of those becomes quadratic too. The recursion also hits Python's limit once list1 has around a thousand elements, so B fails on moderately sized inputs. B's append also returns list2 itself when list1 is empty, which aliases the caller's list. A is simpler, more robust and more idiomatic.
